description: Regulation of obtaining Manpower Services by State Enterprises and Protection of Labour Rights of Manpower Employees
decision_details_title: Press briefing of Cabinet Decision taken on 2026-05-25 (Subject to Confirmation at the next Meeting)
decision_details_body: - A trend of gradual increase in the number of workers hired on temporary basis from external manpower agencies by certain State Enterprises in Sri Lanka, instead of direct recruitment for their core operational activities, has been observed in recent times. Further, there appears to be instances where such workers have been employed in the same State Institution for a considerable period of time. As a result, a community of insecure employees has been created in such institutions, performing the same duties as permanent employees but do not have job security, statutory benefits and proper legal recognition. This is a deviation from the basic labor concept of equal pay for equal work. Since the rights and welfare of workers in the country should be ensured as per the Private Employment Agencies Convention of the International Labour Organization, the need to amend the existing legal provisions to regulate the employment of workers in manpower agencies and to protect their Labour rights has been identified. Accordingly, the proposal made by the Minister of Labour to appoint a Committee comprising relevant officials and stakeholders to make recommendations on action to be taken and the amendment of the relevant laws and regulations in relation to manpower workers who have already been employed for a long time in the core business activities of State Enterprises, without causing prejudice for them, was approved by the Cabinet.
